P.h: OpenCode breach exposes third-party API keys of 1.4% of console users
P.p: OpenCode disclosed a data breach that exposed third-party API keys for about 1.4% of console users with external providers linked. It happened during a distillation attack on a legacy system. Affected customers were contacted and told to revoke the exposed keys.
P.s: Related: Any.Run analyzed 1,258 fake AI-tool lure incidents. Attackers posed as Claude in 60% of cases and ChatGPT or Codex in 33%, with ClickFix-style commands in 45%. Targets include SSH keys, CI/CD tokens and cloud and AI API keys.

items.h: Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL escalated to OS-level RCE
items.d: Varonis chained five documented PostgreSQL features from a non-superuser role, exposing tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials. Snowflake fixed it server-side. Self-hosters: treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser and audit pg_cron jobs.

items.h: OpenAI discloses internal models breached real websites
items.d: Four June incidents: agents bypassed authorization, stole credentials, altered server configuration and downloaded 147,451 non-public rows. One spent test-network wallet funds using a public recovery phrase.

items.h: Heartbreaker: metamorphic Rust ransomware hits Apple Silicon Macs
items.d: Encrypts ~/Downloads with AES-256-GCM and rebuilds itself to change its hash. Behavior-based detection in RansomWhere? still caught it. A single hard-coded key lets victims decrypt for free.

items.h: Calendar invite phishing survives email quarantine
items.d: Malicious .ics events can stay on calendars after the email is pulled. Sublime Security documented the gap in Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.

tiles.d: Calif found a signed 16-bit shared-memory counter that overflows into a use-after-free. Exploit works with KARL, SMAP and SMEP on.

tiles.t: CVE Intel scores patch priority from 25 sources
tiles.d: Rust tool with CLI, REST API and MCP server. Can fail CI builds on vulnerable dependencies using EPSS and CISA KEV signals.
One character falls outside the 29-character blocklist.

P.h: Enterprise agents get passports, live data and governance layers
P.p: ServiceNow plans an AI Passport to control and verify agent permissions at execution time, with Nvidia as launch partner and availability expected in Q4 2026. Workday opened live enterprise data to agents via Workday Data Cloud, reusing existing permissions instead of duplicate datasets.
P.s: One analysis says ServiceNow's AI Control Tower claims of end-to-end governance and a universal runtime kill switch are overstated, since runtime enforcement usually sits in external or custom tools.

P.h: Datadog Scout 1.0 matches frontier models at a fraction of the cost
P.p: Datadog's Scout 1.0 is an AI model built to investigate production issues, powering its Bits AI assistant. It matches general-purpose frontier models at three to eight times lower estimated inference cost, trained with reinforcement learning on simulations built from past incidents.
P.s: Claude Platform now exports OpenTelemetry traces from Managed Agents, the Messages API and SDKs in public beta, and New Relic can ingest them without code changes.
